what_worked: Reverse-engineering the 30-day pricing formula and then testing the counter-hypothesis with p-values is genuinely original.
fix_next: Reconcile slide 3 concentration figures with the dataset's actual top-10 share (49.6%), and clarify whether category medians are seller-only subsets.
verdict: Exceptional thesis, strong arc, honest limitations; a few concentration figures need reconciliation.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: top-1% share stated as 50.6% and top-10% as 84.7%; reference top-10 share is 49.6%, so the 50.6% for top-1% alone seems implausible or uses a different grouping. Slide 9: several category median MRRs diverge from reference medians (e.g., Mobile Apps $223 vs reference $232.50, AI $446 vs $503) without clarifying these may be seller-only or MRR vs revenue figures.

evidence.insight: Slide 5 reverse-engineers pricing as MRR×12 (87.6% match), slide 6 ranks six Spearman correlations showing growth is statistically zero in pricing, slide 7 rejects the 'list on a strong month' hypothesis with p=0.012/0.005, slide 8 shows inverse multiple-revenue relationship. Each builds on the prior finding.
evidence.narrative: Clean arc: market shape (3) → who sells (4) → how pricing works (5) → core finding (6) → counter-hypothesis rejected (7) → multiple compression (8) → category exits (9-10) → zero-revenue listings (11) → actionable trade (12) → six named limitations (13). Single thesis sustained across 13 slides.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 scopes to 1,000 businesses/262 for sale/218 priced. Slide 2 explains API-verified provenance and three trust tiers. Slide 13 devotes a full page to six specific limitations including survivorship bias, asking vs closed prices, small samples, causal discipline, and platform selection bias.
evidence.accuracy: 216 zero-revenue matches reference. 1,000 rows correct. Statistical reporting (Spearman rho, p-values, sample sizes on every chart) is transparent. However, slide 3 concentration figures (50.6% top 1%) cannot be reconciled with reference top-10 share of 49.6%. Category median MRRs on slide 9 differ modestly from reference medians without noting whether these are MRR vs 12-month revenue or seller-only subsets.
evidence.visual: Consistent warm palette with dark/light alternation creating rhythm. Strong typographic hierarchy. Hatched bar for n=5 on slide 8 is effective uncertainty signaling. Horizontal Spearman chart on slide 6 is clean and well-annotated. Sample sizes and confidence labels on every chart. No chartjunk or decorative elements.
